account:
It is day 1, shortly after ten, and I am at the mill for my scheduled grain inspection. I reviewed my appointment books this morning. The secretary reported no incoming letters, grain reports, or other business to her knowledge. My later engagements include council letters at thirteen, tea with the neighbour at fifteen, office time at sixteen thirty, and an additional meeting with the neighbour at town hall at eighteen. The neighbour called that an ordinary meeting; I have no evidence of another purpose.

The unusual news is a repeated, vague report of a bridge or port change at the bakery. Townsfolk 01 and Townsfolk 11 have both repeated it, naming the baker, freight, innkeeper, builder, and neighbour as people who were there. They also reported the innkeeper carrying a sack of bread at the bakery. I have not witnessed the gathering or any change to a bridge or port, and these repeated reports may come from the same circulating story rather than independent observations. I did see the baker nearby carrying a sack of bread and holding an emerald, which by itself could be ordinary bakery business.

I do not yet know what the reported change is for. It might concern transport or deliveries, potentially relevant to grain and bread, but that is only a possibility. My request for someone to show the grain stores and explain supply or delivery problems has not yet produced a substantive answer; instead I received the same bakery report. I should seek firsthand clarification from the named participants rather than treat the rumour as an established plan.
